research_mode: official ONS and Police.uk web sources only; survey quality, methodology, offence-scope and approximate-location guards; no target parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Crime in England and Wales Quality and Methodology Information
verified_claims: the official QMI was last revised on 23 July 2026
the CSEW is a face-to-face survey of around 31000 people aged 16 or over while police recorded crime is administrative data
the provisional CSEW response rate for year ending March 2026 is 48 percent
CSEW estimates are accredited official statistics while most police recorded crime statistics are not accredited because of quality and consistency concerns
around 42 percent of CSEW-comparable crimes were reported to police in year ending March 2026
limitations: neither CSEW nor police recorded crime is a complete count of all crime
survey, administrative and deprivation evidence must remain separate and cannot be collapsed into a cardinal parcel safety probability

sources.name: Crime and justice methodology index
verified_claims: the official methodology index was last revised on 9 June 2026
it provides the current ONS routes for crime user guides methodological notes questionnaires and statistical assessments
limitations: an index page is a discovery and version-control source rather than parcel evidence
each linked methodology or dataset must be independently edition-pinned before use

sources.name: Evaluation of the Crime Survey for England and Wales Panel Design Test
verified_claims: the official evaluation was last revised on 10 March 2026
response attrition reduced effective sample size and raised non-response-bias concerns
later-wave estimates were around 10 percent higher than Wave 1 alone but most differences were not statistically significant
panel and interview-mode effects could not be separated in the experiment
limitations: experimental panel results must not replace the accredited cross-sectional series
national survey-design effects cannot be assigned to an exact parcel or LSOA

sources.name: Crime Survey for England and Wales data quality review
verified_claims: the official review quantifies 95 percent confidence intervals standard errors and coefficients of variation
the year ending March 2023 survey could detect a 4.9 percent change at the 95 percent confidence level compared with 4 percent for year ending March 2020
robbery and theft-from-the-person estimates had lower precision because of low respondent counts
limitations: national survey precision does not establish confidence for a parcel-level candidate
low-volume offence estimates require wider uncertainty and must not be treated as stable small-area rates

sources.name: Nature of crime: violence
verified_claims: the official dataset was released on 26 March 2026
the current listed edition covers year ending March 2025
the CSEW tables include when and where incidents happened and victim perceptions
limitations: annual survey context is not an exact geocoded incident register
victim perception and national survey estimates cannot be assigned to a parcel

sources.name: Nature of crime: fraud and computer misuse
verified_claims: the official dataset was released on 26 March 2026
the current listed edition covers year ending March 2025
year ending March 2021 and March 2022 evidence came from the Telephone-operated Crime Survey
limitations: survey mode and reference period must be preserved across comparisons
fraud and computer misuse are not spatially attributable to an exact property from these tables

sources.name: Nature of crime: robbery
verified_claims: the official dataset was released on 26 March 2026
the current listed edition covers year ending March 2025
the CSEW tables include injuries weapons offender characteristics and victim perceptions
limitations: robbery is a low-volume survey category with higher uncertainty
harm context and victim perception cannot be converted into an exact parcel crime probability

sources.name: Stop and searches by area API contract
verified_claims: the official endpoint supports a one-mile point search or a custom polygon with an optional YYYY-MM month
returned stop-and-search locations are approximations and are not exact event locations
limitations: stop-and-search activity is not a crime-incidence or parcel-safety measure
approximate police-activity locations must not be combined with parcel crime candidates as exact observations
